dependencies.contract: E02 rotates maps and always clears index; E03 validates identity. Parent stop clamps start to range_start, selects less iff detector bullish, supplies bound _search_parent_stop and maps non-null event to main index. Parent type is not a search-key component; parent decision_event_time and normalized price feed start/level. Order stop uses separate per-detector (start,level) membership cache including None; hit still validates E03; miss clamps start and supplies less iff order_direction != bearish. With normal opposite direction, both callback predicates are same trend direction; shared key is conditional on equivalent provider semantics. Both native callbacks bisect lower times at start/end, seek first strict crossing, return exact lower timestamp or None; indexed result (even None) is authoritative, no scan retry. Linear fallback normalizes selected low/high. _extreme_between maps both boundary instants to main positions, clamps to detector range and raises end to start if inverted; whole boundary candle OHLC included, no partial lower clipping. _zone consumes prospective source before ownership rejection. Optional continuation switches only when non-null; nonlive route separate.

LowerTimeframeIndex constructor retains candles reference, copies timestamps, defaults crossing retention off, builds power-of-two segment tree for both extrema, normalizes lows/highs with imported as_decimal, stores sequence position separately. Parent aggregation chooses left on equality; range query compares numeric extremes then earliest position, including cross-segment ties. Range query rejects left<0, right>length, left>=right, absent valid result. No rounding of chosen value. First crossing clamps positions, excludes Low>=level or High<=level, descends earliest eligible segment, optional index-owned retained crossing history (not E cache). Chronology retains aligned main/lower sequences; main_index uses bisect_right-1 and lower clamp, not nearest time. E05 does not invoke refresh_suffix; provider index stability and exact alignment conditional.
Decimal helper returns existing Decimal unchanged, otherwise Decimal(str(value)). E04 level key uses numeric equality not string; E05 returns provider Decimal, not a local conversion.

Optional live continuation is forwarded only when present. Observed native live worker route calls prepare_pipeline_state without live argument, so do not equate live transport with active E04/E05 continuation. Dynamic callers must advance correct chronology and supply valid dirty evidence; no new cross-owner acceptance.
Live transport retains buckets and market views and invokes calculate_live_from_buckets. This does not establish direct E04/E05 dispatch.

limitations: Separate source-first local review by GPT, not independently staffed. Existing AST inventories compared directly, not regenerated.
Local source-only coverage; no RAW, runtime, ZIP, new cross-owner acceptance or production change.

Correct dirty evidence, equivalent callback semantics for equal keys, stable candle/timestamp alignment, comparable finite Decimal prices and normal index bounds are conditional provider/caller requirements; malformed/custom inputs may diverge or raise, not asserted present.

No independent SHA-256 assertion; Git object identities and readback are publication checks. Native live transport does not establish active E continuation; no empirical cache-versus-full-recompute equivalence claimed.
